data.title: Conflicting feedback across different interviewers
data.content:
# Conflicting feedback across different interviewers

Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove bad faith; it shows the rubric was not calibrated across the hiring committee.
data.summary: Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

probes.action: Ask the talent partner for the consolidated rubric summary.
probes.expected_signal: Shows whether the two rounds were scoring against different criteria.

outcomes.label: A summary comes back naming what each round scored, and the two lines about depth turn out to be scores on two different exercises.
outcomes.because: Different criteria across distinct rounds establish separate evaluation dimensions rather than noisy evaluator disagreement.

outcomes.label: A summary comes back naming what each round scored, and both rounds scored the same criterion and recorded opposite results.
outcomes.because: Opposing scores on the identical criterion within the same interview loop demonstrate high inter-rater noise (M-019) rather than an honest calibrated verdict.

outcomes.label: A reply arrives that adds nothing to the decision already sent: the two verdicts restated, or the scoring described as internal and not shared with candidates.
No reply arrives, and no summary is produced.

specimens.label: Two rounds, two verdicts
specimens.subject: Consolidated feedback

lines.text: Round 2 (systems): Strong architectural depth. Reasoned clearly about consistency trade-offs and failure modes. Recommend proceed.
Round 4 (technical): Insufficient depth for the level. Struggled to move past a first-pass solution. Recommend do not proceed.

specimens.reading: Both notes are about the same person in the same week. At least one of them is measuring something other than the candidate.

specimens.label: What the two rounds actually asked

lines.speaker: Interviewer B
lines.text: Round 2 — Walk me through how you would keep two regions in sync when the link between them drops.

lines.speaker: Interviewer D
lines.text: Round 4 — Here is a string parsing problem. You have twenty-five minutes.

specimens.reading: The rounds did not disagree about the candidate; they measured different things and reported both as depth.

perspectives.sees: Two verdicts from the same week: one round rating architectural depth highly, another finding depth insufficient for the level, and one negative decision under them.
perspectives.reads: The rounds asked different questions and both reported the answer as depth. Which of the two the decision rests on is not stated.
perspectives.does: Asks for the consolidated rubric summary, and records what each round actually asked alongside what each concluded.

perspectives.sees: Two written notes on the same candidate from rounds they did not sit in, each using the word depth for a different exercise.
perspectives.reads: Those notes are the whole of what is available about those rounds; nothing in them separates a disagreement about the candidate from a difference between the two exercises.
perspectives.does: Sets who interviews and what each round asks, and closes the split with a decision rather than a re-run. A hire made over a recorded negative note carries their name if it goes wrong.

perspectives.sees: Two recommendations pointing opposite ways and a decision line under them. The scores behind each recommendation are not in the recruiter's view.
perspectives.reads: One reason has to be written to the candidate out of two notes that do not agree. Anything said beyond the recorded decision can be quoted back later.
perspectives.does: Sends the outcome in wording that stays inside what was written down, and moves the requisition on. Reopening a recorded decision sits with the hiring manager, not the recruiter.

non_inferences: Does not prove bad faith; it shows the rubric was not calibrated across the hiring committee.
